//: Copy to honesty_gate.config.json (same dir) or point $HONESTY_GATE_CONFIG at it. Then run `honesty_stop_gate.py --check-config` — it flags any verification command whose binary does not exist on your box.
//claim_patterns: How a live/background-state claim reads in YOUR domain. Regex fragments, OR-joined, matched case-insensitively inside word boundaries. Keep both families: RUNNING-type (is running / in progress / pending) and COMPLETION-type (has completed / is finished).
//completion_pattern: Matches ONLY completion claims (linking verb + done/finished; the adjective-shaped words must be clause-final so 'is complete garbage' does not match). These, when they name no configured subject, are treated as in-turn prose whose output is already in the transcript. Do not drop the linking-verb requirement, or a bare 'Done,' opening a sentence will fire.
//verification_commands: The commands on YOUR box that ACTUALLY OBSERVE live process/service state. THIS IS THE STAIR-TO-NOWHERE SURFACE — `--check-config` verifies each binary resolves here. The gate confirms such a command RAN and NAMED the subject; it does NOT read the command's output, so only list commands whose RUNNING is itself the observation (a process/service probe). File-existence reads (`ls`, `stat`) and log reads (`cat`/`tail` a .log) are deliberately NOT here: a log file exists whether or not the process is alive, so they read as coverage without proving liveness. Add them only if you understand you are asserting content/existence, not that something is running.
//subjects: The named things whose state you assert (your job/service/agent vocabulary). Reduced to the token before the first '-'. A verifying command must NAME the claim's subject to cover it — verifying one subject never licenses a claim about another. Prefer distinct single tokens over generic compounds ('build' and 'job' as separate subjects make 'build job' demand both be verified).
//non_subjects: Words that never name a subject alone, so 'it is still running' does not self-verify. A subjectless RUNNING claim ('both are still running') is treated as uncovered and blocks — it cannot pass off an unrelated probe.
//verify_hint: One line shown in the block message naming how to verify on your stack.
verify_hint: the command that observes this subject's real state (e.g. `pgrep -af <name>`, `systemctl status <svc>`, read the log/artifact)
